destination.name: Rome
destination.tipping: Not expected. Rounding up or leaving 1-2 EUR is a courtesy.
destination.tap_water: Safe. Free public drinking fountains (nasoni) across the city.

entry.summary: Italy is in the Schengen area. The EU Entry/Exit System (biometric registration for non-EU short-stay visitors) has been fully operational at all Schengen external borders since 10 April 2026. ETIAS (pre-travel authorisation for visa-exempt nationals) is expected to start in Q4 2026; the exact date is to be announced and enforcement is expected to follow a transition period. Check official EU pages before you travel.

safety_snapshot.note: The main risks for visitors are pickpocketing and overcharging in tourist areas. Violent crime against tourists is uncommon.

transport.name: Leonardo Express (Fiumicino to Roma Termini)
transport.note: Non-stop, about every 15 min, roughly 05:38-23:27 from the airport. Platforms 23-24 at Termini.

transport.name: Official taxi, Fiumicino to inside the Aurelian Walls
transport.note: Fixed fare per car, supplements included, day or night. Outside the walls the meter applies. Ciampino to centre is a fixed 40 EUR.

transport.name: FL1 regional train (Fiumicino)
transport.note: Does not stop at Termini (stops at Trastevere, Ostiense, Tiburtina). Cheaper, less direct.

transport.name: Metro, bus and tram single ticket
transport.note: Time-limited ticket for buses and trams, one metro ride. Validate on entry or on board.

safety_zones.name: Termini station area
safety_zones.note: Touts, unofficial taxis, ticket-machine 'helpers', pickpockets. Busy and well used, but be careful late at night.

safety_zones.name: Colosseum perimeter
safety_zones.note: Costumed 'gladiator' photo fees, unofficial tour touts, fake skip-the-line sellers.

safety_zones.name: Trevi Fountain and Spanish Steps
safety_zones.note: Dense crowds, pickpockets, rose and bracelet sellers.

safety_zones.name: St. Peter's and Vatican Museums queues
safety_zones.note: Queue touts, overpriced 'skip the line' tours, rosary or blessing hustles.

safety_zones.name: Piazza Navona, Pantheon and Campo de' Fiori restaurants
safety_zones.note: Menus without prices, photo menus, hidden cover and service charges, restaurant touts.

safety_zones.name: Trastevere late-night streets
safety_zones.note: Lively nightlife. Pickpockets and phone snatching are more likely in crowds after dark.

places.name: Colosseum
places.price: Standard ticket about 16 EUR plus 2 EUR online booking fee (Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill on a 24h combo). SUPER ticket about 35 EUR adds the underground and arena floor.
tips: Buy only from the official site (CoopCulture) or the ticket office.
Large bags are not allowed in. Bring ID that matches the ticket name.
places.access: Partial; lifts to the upper tier exist, check current access.

places.name: Roman Forum and Palatine Hill
places.why: The political and religious heart of ancient Rome, with big views from the Palatine.
places.price: Included in the Colosseum combo ticket.
tips: Little shade. Bring water and a hat in summer.

places.name: Pantheon
places.why: Nearly 2,000-year-old temple with the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome.
places.price: A ticket of about 5 EUR for non-residents has applied since 2023; verify current price.
tips: It is a working church. Visits can be limited during Mass.

places.name: Trevi Fountain
places.price: Free to view from the square. Since 2 Feb 2026 non-residents pay 2 EUR to go down to the basin area (timed access, crowd cap).
tips: Pay at the fountain or online to skip the line. Residents are exempt.
places.access: Viewing is step-free from the square; basin access has steps.

places.name: Spanish Steps
places.why: Iconic baroque staircase leading to Trinita dei Monti church.
tips: Stand or walk. Sitting on the steps can be fined.
places.access: Stairs; a lift is available nearby at the Spagna metro station.

places.name: Piazza Navona
places.why: Baroque square with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers.
tips: Drink prices on the square are high. Walk two streets away to eat.

places.name: Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel
places.why: Vast papal art collections ending in Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel.
places.price: Ticket about 17 EUR; online reservation brings it to about 22 EUR. Special Friday evening openings in the warm months cost more.
tips: Closed most Sundays (free last Sunday, extremely crowded). Check the official calendar.
Photography is not allowed in the Sistine Chapel.
Exception: the museums open free on the last Sunday of the month (verify), with very long queues.

places.name: St. Peter's Basilica
places.why: The largest church in Christendom, with Michelangelo's dome.
places.price: Entry is free. The dome climb is paid.
tips: Shoulders and knees must be covered. Security queue can be long.

places.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
places.why: Hadrian's mausoleum turned papal fortress with rooftop views.
tips: Walk the Ponte Sant'Angelo at sunset for free.

places.name: Capitoline Museums
places.why: One of the world's oldest public museums; great view over the Forum.
places.price: Non-residents pay an admission fee since 1 Feb 2026 (exact price: verify). Residents of the Rome metropolitan area enter free.
tips: Michelangelo's Campidoglio square is free.

places.name: Galleria Borghese
places.why: Bernini and Caravaggio masterpieces in an intimate villa.
tips: Entry is by timed reservation only, in about two-hour slots. Arrive 20 minutes early.

places.name: Villa Borghese gardens
places.why: Rome's central park: bike rental, rowing lake, Pincio terrace sunset view.
tips: Walk up to the Pincio terrace for Piazza del Popolo views.

places.name: Trastevere
places.why: Cobbled lanes, trattorie and lively evenings.
tips: Book dinner. Eat away from the main square.

places.name: Campo de' Fiori
tips: Souvenir-style stalls; compare prices.

places.name: Testaccio Market
places.why: Local food market with street-food stalls (supplì, sandwiches, pizza).
places.price: Free entry; food from about 3-12 EUR.
tips: Mostly a morning market; check days and hours.

places.name: Janiculum Hill (Gianicolo)
places.why: One of Rome's best free panoramas, with a noon cannon tradition.
tips: Walk up from Trastevere (about 20 minutes uphill).

places.name: Baths of Caracalla
tips: A good quieter alternative to the Forum crowds.

places.name: Appian Way Regional Park
places.why: Ancient road lined with tombs and catacombs; walk or bike.
tips: Much of the road is closed to cars on Sundays and holidays; check.

food.name: The Roman pasta four
food.desc: Carbonara (guanciale, egg, pecorino; no cream), cacio e pepe (pecorino and pepper), amatriciana (guanciale, tomato, pecorino), gricia (carbonara without egg).
food.tip: Cream in carbonara is not traditional. Menus with photos and touts outside are a warning sign.

food.name: Supplì and pizza al taglio
food.desc: Fried rice croquettes with melted mozzarella; Roman pizza sold by weight.
food.tip: Check the price per 100 g (etto) before the slice is cut and weighed.
food.price_eur: supplì 1.5-3; pizza al taglio 2.5-6 a slice

food.name: Roscioli Salumeria con Cucina
food.desc: Deli and restaurant famed for carbonara and cured meats.
food.tip: Reserve ahead. Confirm it is open before listing publicly.

food.name: Da Enzo al 29
food.desc: Small family trattoria known for Roman classics.
food.tip: Expect a queue; confirm booking policy.

food.name: Felice a Testaccio
food.desc: Known for cacio e pepe tossed at the table.

food.name: Pizzarium (Bonci)
food.desc: Creative pizza al taglio near the Vatican Museums.
food.tip: Good lunch stop after the museums.

food.name: Giolitti
food.tip: Pay at the cashier first, then show the receipt at the counter.

food.name: Sant'Eustachio Il Caffe
food.tip: Standing at the bar costs less than a table.

food.name: Pasticceria Regoli
food.desc: Old-school bakery known for maritozzi (cream-filled buns).

food.name: Coperto and service charge
food.desc: A per-person cover charge is common and legal when shown on the menu. A separate service charge may also appear. Tipping beyond that is optional.
food.tip: Check the menu footer before ordering. Ask for the total if prices are listed by weight.

hidden_spots.name: Aventine Keyhole
hidden_spots.why: Peek through a keyhole in the Knights of Malta priory door to see St. Peter's dome framed by a hedge.
hidden_spots.etiquette: Quiet residential square. Be brief and respectful.

hidden_spots.name: Giardino degli Aranci (Orange Garden)
hidden_spots.why: Calm terrace with sweeping views over Rome, much quieter than the Janiculum at peak times.

hidden_spots.name: Quartiere Coppede
hidden_spots.why: Fantastical early-20th-century architecture mixing Art Nouveau and medieval styles.

hidden_spots.name: Basilica di San Clemente
hidden_spots.why: Three layers of history: medieval church over a 4th-century church over a Roman house and a Mithraic temple.

hidden_spots.name: Garbatella
hidden_spots.why: Garden-city neighborhood of courtyards and murals where locals live.
hidden_spots.etiquette: Residential courtyards: no loud groups or drones.

scams.title: Unofficial taxi or inflated fare from the airport or Termini
scams.how: A man offers a 'taxi' inside the terminal. The car has no meter, no license number or a fake one, and the price is agreed after you are inside.
scams.avoid: Use the official white taxis at the rank. From Fiumicino to inside the Aurelian Walls the fare is fixed at 55 EUR. Or take the 14 EUR Leonardo Express.
scams.if_happened: Note the plate and time. Report to the local police or Polizia Locale and to your card issuer if you paid by card.

scams.title: Costumed 'gladiators' demand a photo fee
scams.how: Costumed performers pose with you, then insist on a high payment, sometimes pressuring a group.
scams.avoid: Decline politely and keep walking. If you take a photo, agree on a price first.
scams.if_happened: Do not argue. Pay a small agreed amount if you feel unsafe, then report persistent harassment to police.

scams.title: Skip-the-line touts and fake tickets
scams.how: Touts near entrances sell 'skip-the-line' tours or tickets at inflated prices, sometimes unofficial or invalid.
scams.avoid: Book timed tickets online from the official site in advance. A licensed guide will not approach you on the street.
scams.if_happened: Keep receipts and screenshots. Ask the seller's bank or card issuer for a dispute.

scams.title: Tourist-trap restaurants and hidden charges
scams.how: Menus without prices, photo menus, fish or steak priced per 100 g (etto) without a stated total, large cover and service charges.
scams.avoid: Read the full menu and footer. Ask for the total before ordering weighed items. Eat two or three streets away from major squares.
scams.if_happened: Ask for an itemised receipt (scontrino). You can report overcharging to Polizia Locale.

scams.title: Pickpockets in crowds and on buses
scams.how: Teams use crowding and distraction on buses, the metro and at major sights.
scams.avoid: Keep bags zipped and in front. Do not keep phones in back pockets. Be extra careful on crowded buses to the Vatican.
scams.if_happened: Block your cards, report to police (and get a report for insurance), and use Find My Device.

scams.title: 'Free' roses, bracelets or gifts
scams.how: A seller hands you a rose or ties a bracelet, then demands money.
scams.avoid: Keep your hands free, say no clearly and keep walking.
scams.if_happened: Do not engage. Return the item if possible.

scams.title: Ticket-machine 'helpers'
scams.how: Helpers operate the machine for you, then demand payment or switch the change.
scams.avoid: Decline help. Use machines carefully or buy at staffed windows or apps.

scams.title: Rosary or 'blessing' hustle near the Vatican
scams.how: Someone offers a rosary or a blessing and then asks for a donation.
scams.avoid: Decline politely. Only trust official Vatican staff and posted information.

scams.title: Dynamic currency conversion at ATMs and card terminals
scams.how: The machine offers to charge you in your home currency at a poor rate.
scams.avoid: Always choose to pay in euros.
scams.if_happened: Ask your bank about the fee and check your statement.

scams.title: Fake QR code stickers
scams.how: A sticker covers a genuine QR code on a menu, parking meter or kiosk and sends you to a payment page that steals card details.
scams.avoid: Check for stickers placed over printed codes and prefer official apps and sites.

rules.title: Entry and EU border systems
rules.summary: Italy is in Schengen. The EU Entry/Exit System has been fully in operation since 10 April 2026. ETIAS is expected in Q4 2026 and is not yet confirmed as required.
rules.instead: Check your nationality's visa and ETIAS status on the official EU site before booking.

rules.title: No sitting on the Spanish Steps
rules.summary: Rome municipal rules ban sitting or lounging on the Spanish Steps. Press reports describe fines of about 250 EUR for sitting and up to about 400 EUR for dirtying or damaging them. Amounts differ between sources.
rules.instead: Rest on benches nearby or at the Pincio terrace.

rules.title: Do not wade or bathe in fountains
rules.summary: Entering the water of Rome's monumental fountains is prohibited and finable, with penalties reported in the hundreds of euros.
rules.instead: Throw a coin from the allowed distance and enjoy the view.

rules.title: Trevi Fountain access fee for non-residents
rules.summary: Since 2 February 2026, non-residents pay 2 EUR to access the basin area near the Trevi Fountain. Viewing from the square remains free. Residents of Rome and some groups are exempt.
rules.instead: Buy online to skip the queue or view from the square for free.

rules.title: No messy eating at monuments
rules.summary: Local rules ban 'messy eating' on monument steps and around some historic sites.
rules.instead: Eat in a cafe, park or piazza designated for it.

rules.title: Cover shoulders and knees in churches
rules.summary: St. Peter's, the Vatican Museums and many churches enforce a dress code: shoulders and knees covered.
rules.instead: Carry a light scarf or shawl.

rules.title: Security checks and bag rules
rules.summary: Major sights have airport-style screening and may refuse large bags or sharp objects.
rules.instead: Travel light and check each site's prohibited-items list.

rules.title: Timed reservations at popular sites
rules.summary: The Borghese Gallery requires a timed reservation. Colosseum and Vatican entries are strongly recommended in advance.
rules.instead: Reserve online from official sites weeks ahead.

rules.title: Paid guiding may require a licence
rules.summary: Paid guiding at many state-run monuments and museums is regulated and may require a licensed guide. Rules differ by site and are subject to change.
rules.instead: Choose licensed guides for site tours and label informal local companions as such. Needs legal verification before launch.
rules.juris: Italy / Ministry of Culture / Roma Capitale

rules.title: Validate transport tickets
rules.summary: Tickets must be validated on entry or on board where required. Inspectors issue fines to those without a valid ticket.
rules.instead: Validate at the machine and keep your ticket until you exit.

rules.title: Drones are heavily restricted
rules.summary: Flying drones over central Rome is restricted or prohibited without authorisation. Penalties can be serious.
rules.instead: Do not fly in the historic centre. Check Italy's aviation authority (ENAC) rules first.

rules.title: Alcohol and public drinking
rules.summary: The legal purchase age is 18. Some areas restrict takeaway alcohol late at night and public drunkenness can be penalised.

fair_prices.note: Above 20 EUR near major landmarks is a tourist premium.
Avoid giant neon-coloured piles; natural colours and covered metal tubs are better signs.
Legal only if shown on the menu.
Varies with language, licence and group size.

expected_findings.msg: Vatican Museums are closed on most Sundays. Check the official calendar or move to another day.
Galleria Borghese needs a timed reservation and visits last about two hours.
Borghese (10:00, two hours) overlaps with the Colosseum at 10:45 and the cities are 30+ minutes apart.
Late night in a crowded nightlife area raises pickpocket risk. Keep valuables in front pockets, use licensed taxis or night buses.
